candidate.derivedAnswer: A pair of straight lines; choice C.
candidate.answerReason: Factoring gives (x - 2y)(x + 2y) = 0, whose solution set is the union of y = x/2 and y = -x/2.

methods.label: Factor and interpret each branch
methods.explanation:
Because the equation equals zero, factoring lets us separate its solutions into simpler alternatives:
\[
x^2-4y^2=(x-2y)(x+2y)=0.
\]
A product of real numbers is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero. Thus a point lies on the graph exactly when
\[
x-2y=0\qquad\text{or}\qquad x+2y=0.
\]
These equations are \(y=x/2\) and \(y=-x/2\), two distinct straight lines through the origin. Every point on either line satisfies the original equation, so these lines form the entire graph. The answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: Difference-of-squares factoring, the zero-product rule, and recognition of line graphs are elementary school algebra.
